title: Executive Team weekly
summary: Weekly operational meeting of the Executive Team: final run-through before the 15 October board, a proposal to bring Copilot Wave 1 forward to 2 November, the overdue progress review count, P2 month-end, Valemont and the coach recruitment request.
description: Weekly operational meeting of the Delcorn Executive Team (Mondays 09:30–10:30). Action log is kept by the Board Secretary.
agenda: Copilot rollout — readiness and wave dates
People — Wellbeing Week and coach recruitment request

transcript.text: Morning all. Happy Wellbeing Week — and yes, I do see the irony of starting it with an hour on Teams. Let's try to finish early. Oliver, action log?
Morning. Nothing carried over from last week — the away-day actions are either done or in the board pack. So we're starting from a clean sheet.
Apart from my write-up of the away-day whiteboard, which, er... I haven't done. Can I just talk to the photo on Thursday?
Talk to it. It's three lines. Oliver's got the photo. Right — the board. Anything anyone's worried about for Thursday?
Only that Richard will ask about Level 7, and I want us all quoting the same number. Around nine hundred thousand over two years. Not 'about a million', please.
Noted. Nine hundred over two years. Aisha — Copilot, because that's the paper they'll spend longest on.

Thanks. So the paper's in the pack with the three conditions. Permissions remediation is at seventy-nine per cent this morning — Liam's working through the old project sites. The restricted library exclusion is built and we're testing it this week. And Copilot Essentials goes live in the CPD portal on Wednesday.

The ask from me is this. The pilot's gone so well that I'd like to bring Wave 1 forward a week. Central teams and the delivery managers on Monday the second of November, then coaches and tutors on Monday the sixteenth — which is what we wrote on the whiteboard anyway.
The board paper says the ninth, though. Are we going to confuse them?
The conditions get confirmed at the end of October either way. If they're met on the thirtieth, there's no reason to sit on our hands for another week. I'd tell the board verbally.
The sixteenth is a busy week for delivery — Birmingham opens that day, and we're not far off the ILR. But honestly I'd rather coaches had it before Christmas than not.
I'm comfortable. Licence cost is the same whichever Monday it is.
From a comms point of view, we need one set of dates and we stick to them. If we say the second, we mean the second.

Agreed. Let's go with the second and the sixteenth, subject to the go/no-go. Aisha, you'll say that on Thursday. And can someone confirm the Essentials date so Marcus can put it in the managers' briefing?
I'll confirm it with Ellie by Friday.
Lovely. Reviews. David.

So — the number this morning is a hundred and eighty-four learners with an overdue progress review. It was a hundred and seventy-six at the start of the month. It's the September and October start peak landing on coaches who were already over caseload.
QIP-07 is Amber at the moment. If it keeps going this way it'll be Red at the October QIP review.
What's the plan to turn it round? I don't want Imran to be the first person who asks us that.
Rachel's on it. What I'd like to do is bring you a proper trajectory by academy — where we expect to be week by week, and what caseload relief does to it. Give me till next Monday.
Next Monday. Fine.
Priya — P2.

September closed on Friday. Apprenticeship funding was behind budget for the month, so year to date we're about fifty-nine thousand behind. Most of it's Data Academy completion payments where EPA dates moved, so I'm calling it timing for now. R02 went in clean last week.
Keep an eye on October.
I will. If it's two months running I'll want to know why by academy, not just 'fewer starts'.
Tom.

Valemont — Ravi ran the discovery workshop last week and it went really well. The proposal goes on Wednesday: sixteen on AI4, eight on Applied Machine Learning, four hundred and ninety-six thousand of levy, plus commercial add-ons. First starts late January.

Northgrid's QBR is on the twentieth, I'll report back after that. Oh, and the Kestrel case study went live on Friday. Lewis says their Early Careers Manager mentioned something about a depot reorganisation, but nothing that touches us.
Kestrel have forty-one learners on programme. If something's coming I'd like to know early.
Honestly, I think it's noise. I'll keep an ear out.
Marcus.

Two things. Wellbeing Week — please actually go to something, and protect Friday afternoon. No meetings. Second, the recruitment paper. Eight additional coaches ahead of budget, a hundred and eighty-six thousand part-year. Rolling coach turnover is fourteen per cent, so without these we're running to stand still.
I'll brief Catherine on that before Thursday so it isn't a surprise. And Wednesday's risk review, Oliver?
Wednesday at two. I'll drop the updated top risks into the pack straight after, so the board sees the post-review version.
Siân.
Q1 OTJ sampling starts this week — Daniel's taking sixty learners. The October QIP review is on the twenty-third. And Grace says all safeguarding cases are within response standards.
Thank you. AOB? Marcus, Birmingham?
Fit-out's on track for Monday the sixteenth of November. Desk booking will be through the Teams app.
Good. Oliver, can you read the actions back?

David — bring the overdue progress review recovery trajectory to the Executive Team, next Monday. Aisha — confirm the Copilot Essentials go-live date in the CPD portal, by Friday. Helena — brief Catherine on the eight-coach recruitment request before the board. And me — add the updated top risks to the board pack after Wednesday's risk review.
Perfect. Thanks, everyone — now go and do something wellbeing-ish.

recap.summary: In a short Wellbeing Week meeting the Executive Team prepared for the 15 October board. Aisha Karim proposed bringing Copilot Wave 1 forward to Monday 2 November (Wave 2 on 16 November), which the team agreed subject to the end-of-October go/no-go. David Okafor reported 184 overdue progress reviews (176 at the start of October) and will bring a recovery trajectory next week. Priya Raman reported funding about £59,000 behind budget year to date at P2, mostly Data Academy completion timing. Tom Whitfield confirmed the Valemont proposal goes out on 14 October.

topics.title: Board on 15 October
topics.text: Everyone to quote the Level 7 impact as around £0.9m over two years. David Okafor will talk to the away-day whiteboard photo rather than a written paper.

topics.title: Copilot rollout — readiness and wave dates
topics.text: Permissions remediation 79% complete; restricted library exclusion in testing; Copilot Essentials goes live in the CPD portal on Wednesday 14 October. The team agreed to bring Wave 1 forward from the board paper's 9 November to Monday 2 November, with Wave 2 on Monday 16 November, subject to the go/no-go on 30 October.

topics.title: Progress reviews
topics.text: 184 learners have an overdue progress review, up from 176 at the start of October, driven by the autumn start peak. QIP-07 is Amber and at risk of Red. The COO will bring a recovery trajectory by academy.

topics.title: Finance — P2 month-end
topics.text: Apprenticeship funding about £59,000 behind budget year to date, mostly Data Academy completion payments delayed by EPA date changes (timing). R02 submitted cleanly.

topics.title: Commercial, people and quality
topics.text: Valemont AI Academy proposal (£496,000 levy) goes on Wednesday; Northgrid QBR on 20 October. Kestrel's Early Careers Manager mentioned a depot reorganisation — thought to be noise. Coach turnover is 14%; the board will be asked to approve eight additional coaches (£186,000 part-year). Q1 OTJ sampling (60 learners) starts this week. Birmingham hub on track for 16 November.

decisions: Copilot Wave 1 brought forward to Monday 2 November 2026 and Wave 2 set for Monday 16 November, subject to the go/no-go on 30 October; Aisha Karim to tell the board verbally.

actions.action: Bring the overdue progress review recovery trajectory to the Executive Team
Confirm the Copilot Essentials go-live date in the CPD portal
Brief Catherine Ashworth on the eight-coach recruitment request before the board
Add the updated top risks to the board pack after the 14 October risk review

title: Executive Team weekly
summary: Weekly operational meeting of the Executive Team: board debrief, Copilot dates and readiness, overdue progress reviews, the split of the eight board-approved coach posts, Northgrid and Valemont. Siân Llewellyn sent apologies.
description: Weekly operational meeting of the Delcorn Executive Team (Mondays 09:30–10:30). Action log is kept by the Board Secretary.

transcript.text: Morning. Siân's sent apologies — she's at the EPAO forum today — and Oliver has her update. Oliver, action log.

Four from last week. Helena briefed Catherine on the recruitment request — done. I added the post-review top risks to the board pack — done. Aisha confirmed the Essentials date — it went live on Wednesday, so done. And David's trajectory, which—
Which isn't ready, sorry. Kate's rebuilding the caseload model after the October intake and I don't want to bring you a trajectory built on last month's caseloads. Next week.
Next week, David. Properly.

Board debrief, briefly. Copilot approved subject to the three conditions. Eight coaches approved. Level 7 mitigation endorsed. Richard wants a Q1 trading update by the sixth of November — that's on the board action log for Priya. And Imran pushed hard on overdue reviews; the board wants a timeliness trajectory in January.
And the audit sign-off is at Audit and Risk on the third of December. Thank you all for the Level 7 discipline, by the way. Nobody said a million.
Ha. Aisha — the minute says a target go-live of the ninth. Where does that leave the second?

It says the ninth because that's what the paper said. I told them we'd like to start Wave 1 on the second if the conditions are confirmed on the thirtieth, and Catherine was relaxed as long as we don't cut corners. So we stay on the second and the sixteenth. The FAQ and the Champions channel already say that.
Just flagging — if the board minute says the ninth and our comms say the second, someone's going to spot it.
The draft minute records the resolution as it was passed. I'll mention it to Catherine, but I can't change what the board resolved.
Fine. We hold the second and the sixteenth. Readiness, Aisha?
Permissions remediation's at eighty-eight per cent. Essentials is live. And — gently — two of the eight of us have done it. Oliver and me.
Point taken. I'd like every one of us done before we make the go-live decision, so by the go/no-go on the thirtieth. I'll own chasing it.
I'll do mine this week. Promise.
David — the reviews number, at least.
A hundred and ninety-one this morning. Still rising, about seven a week. Rachel's got Red learners being re-booked first, and it's top of the agenda at Wednesday's delivery team meeting.
Okay. I want the trajectory next week.
Marcus — the eight posts.

So, now we have approval I want adverts out this week. My proposal for the split: five Data and three Leadership. That's where the caseloads are. Some Data coaches are over a hundred and fifteen per cent, and Kwame's on thirty.
No AI at all? With Valemont in the pipeline?
Three new AI4 coaches joined this month, and Owen Lacey starts as an AI coach on the sixteenth of November. AI is the one academy that isn't over target.
I'm with Marcus. The pain is Data and Leadership.
Tom, I hear you, but we recruit for the problem we've got, not the one we might have. Five Data, three Leadership. Marcus, adverts by Friday.
And I'll phase the part-year cost — the hundred and eighty-six thousand — into the forecast by Friday as well, so it's in the P3 reforecast.
Thanks. Priya, anything else on money?
R03 is the fifth of November. October looks like it'll be behind again, but I'll know more once Tom's been to Northgrid.
Tom.

Northgrid QBR is tomorrow. I'm fairly sure the Data Analyst cohort is going to move — their Network Analytics team is restructuring and the line managers aren't confirmed. I'll come back with the new date. Valemont went on Wednesday; Sally Miah's taking it to their exec this week.
And Kestrel? Laura said on Friday that two Kestrel line managers cancelled reviews last week, and one of them told the coach he doesn't know if he'll have a job in January.
Ah. That'll be the depot reorganisation. Lewis is seeing them at the end of the month — I'll ask him to dig.
Keep it on the radar, please.

Siân's update: Q1 OTJ sampling is under way, sixty learners, draft findings by the end of the month. The QIP review is on Friday the twenty-third. And Grace says all safeguarding cases are within response standards.
Thank you. AOB — Birmingham?
Desk booking opens on the ninth of November. Jess has the Hub article ready to go.
Great. Oliver, read them back.

David — bring the overdue progress review recovery trajectory to the Executive Team, next Monday. Marcus — launch adverts for the eight additional coach posts, by Friday. Priya — phase the £186,000 part-year cost of the eight coach posts into the FY2026/27 forecast, by Friday. Tom — confirm the revised start date for the Northgrid Data Analyst cohort after the QBR. And Helena — all Executive Team members to complete Copilot Essentials before the go/no-go on the thirtieth.
Lovely. Thanks all.

recap.summary: Helena Marsh debriefed the 15 October board: Copilot approved subject to three conditions, eight additional coaches approved, Level 7 mitigation endorsed and a Q1 trading update requested by Meridian for 6 November. The team kept Copilot Wave 1 on 2 November and Wave 2 on 16 November, although the board minute records a 9 November target. Overdue progress reviews rose to 191; the COO's recovery trajectory slipped a week. The team agreed to split the eight coach posts five Data and three Leadership, with no AI post. Siân Llewellyn sent apologies.

topics.title: Action log
topics.text: Three of last week's four actions complete (Catherine briefed, top risks added to the board pack, Copilot Essentials live since 14 October). The overdue review trajectory slipped to 26 October while the caseload model is rebuilt.

topics.title: Board debrief
topics.text: Copilot rollout approved subject to the three conditions; eight coaches approved (£186,000 part-year); Level 7 mitigation endorsed; Meridian wants a Q1 trading update by 6 November; the board wants a review-timeliness trajectory in January. Audit sign-off at the Audit & Risk Committee on 3 December.

topics.title: Copilot dates and readiness
topics.text: The board minute records a 9 November target, but the Exec will start Wave 1 on 2 November and Wave 2 on 16 November if the conditions are confirmed on 30 October. Permissions remediation is 88% complete. Only two of the eight Executive Team members have completed Copilot Essentials.

topics.title: Progress reviews
topics.text: 191 learners have an overdue progress review, rising by about seven a week. Red learners are being re-booked first; it is top of the agenda at the 21 October delivery team meeting.

topics.title: Eight additional coach posts
topics.text: Split agreed as five Data Academy and three Leadership Academy, with no AI post, because AI took on three new coaches in October and Owen Lacey starts on 16 November. Adverts due by 23 October; the CFO will phase the £186,000 into the forecast.

topics.title: Finance, commercial and quality
topics.text: October funding is likely to be behind again. The Northgrid QBR is on 20 October and the Data Analyst cohort is expected to move. Valemont is reviewing the proposal. Two Kestrel line managers cancelled reviews amid a depot reorganisation. OTJ sampling is under way and the QIP review is on 23 October.

decisions: Copilot dates held at Wave 1 Monday 2 November and Wave 2 Monday 16 November, despite the board minute's 9 November target.
The eight additional skills coach posts are split five Data Academy and three Leadership Academy, with no AI Academy post.
Every Executive Team member to complete Copilot Essentials before the 30 October go/no-go.

actions.action: Bring the overdue progress review recovery trajectory to the Executive Team
Launch adverts for the eight additional coach posts
Phase the £186,000 part-year cost of the eight coach posts into the FY2026/27 forecast
Confirm the revised start date for the Northgrid Data Analyst cohort after the QBR

title: Executive Team weekly
summary: Weekly operational meeting of the Executive Team: slipped actions on coach adverts, budget phasing and the review trajectory, Copilot go/no-go preparation, overdue reviews and QIP-07 going Red, Northgrid and Valemont, and Kestrel pausing November starts.
description: Weekly operational meeting of the Delcorn Executive Team (Mondays 09:30–10:30). Action log is kept by the Board Secretary.

transcript.text: Morning. Tom's on a train — he says he'll join when he gets signal somewhere past Milton Keynes. Oliver, action log.
Five from last week. Tom confirmed the Northgrid date — I'll let him give it when he's on. Marcus, adverts?
Not out, I'm afraid. Joe's ready and the copy's approved, but the posts need cost-centre codes in PeopleFlow before they can go live, and those are waiting on the budget phasing.
That's mine. I can get Joe the cost codes today — that doesn't need to wait. The phasing itself I'd rather do after P3 close, so... end of this week.
So the adverts can go this week regardless?
Thursday. I'll confirm in the chat.
David — the trajectory?
I've got Rachel's draft, but she's about to ask both delivery managers for recovery plans by coach and I'd rather bring you the version with the plans in. Next Monday. I know, I know.
David, that's the third week. I'm going to stop asking nicely.
Fair.
And Copilot Essentials for this group — Aisha?
Five of the eight. Helena, David and Priya still to do.
Guilty as charged. By Friday. Moving on.
Copilot. Aisha, where are we for Friday?

Permissions remediation is at ninety-four per cent. The last few are old project sites with 'Everyone except external users'. Restricted libraries are excluded and tested, and Essentials is live and mandatory. Liam's re-running the data access governance report on Wednesday as a final sweep before I write the go/no-go recommendation. Dates are still Wave 1 on the second, Wave 2 on the sixteenth.
On the sixteenth — I'm getting nervous. That's the week of the November ILR data freeze, and Birmingham opens the same day. Coaches will be cleansing ILR data and learning Copilot at the same time.
It could be argued either way. Can we take it in the go/no-go thread, with Liam's results in front of us?
Yes. For now the dates stand — the second and the sixteenth — and we make the final call on Friday. David, put your concern in the thread.
Will do.
Reviews.

A hundred and ninety-eight this morning, seven up on last week. Rachel took it to the team on Wednesday: Red learners first, and a new rule that a nominated workplace mentor can attend if the line manager cancels twice.
And I should say QIP-07 went Red at Friday's QIP review. It's the second Red, alongside OTJ.
Then that's the trajectory I want next week, David. With dates on it.
Sorry — I'm here. Can you hear me? I've got about four minutes before a tunnel.
Quick, Tom. Northgrid and Valemont.

Northgrid: as I feared, the Data Analyst cohort's moved. Twelve starts, now Monday the eleventh of January. I'm trying to get in front of their Chief Digital Officer. Valemont: Sally Miah wants to go to twenty on AI4 — that's another seventy-six thousand of levy, five hundred and seventy-two in total — and their People Committee decides on the twelfth of November. Which is why I want to reopen the coach split. If Valemont lands, we've got twenty AI4 starts in January and no new AI coach.
The adverts are about to go out as five and three.
I don't want to hold the adverts up again. Marcus, can they go out without fixing the numbers per academy?
Yes — we can advertise the Data and Leadership roles as 'several posts', and add an AI one if we need it.
Then that's what we do, and we revisit the split properly next Monday.
One more — Kestrel. Their Early Careers Manager told Lewis on Friday that the November starts are on hold while they restructure the depots. Six learners. Current learners are fine, for now.
That's forty-one on programme and two cancelled reviews already. I need to know whether it's a pause or a stop.
I'll find out by Friday — sorry, you're breaking up, I'll drop off and read the recap.
Thanks, Tom. Priya.
P3 close starts next week. With Northgrid moving, October funding will be behind again, mostly in the Data Academy. I'll have proper numbers for R03 on the fifth.
Siân.
The OTJ audit draft is due on Friday. Early sight: no ineligible claims, but the catch-up plans for behind-plan learners look thin. And all safeguarding cases are within response standards.
Thank you. AOB — I'll be at the Birmingham coffee morning on the sixteenth, so please don't book me anything that morning. Oliver, actions.

David — bring the overdue progress review recovery trajectory to the Executive Team, next Monday. Priya — phase the £186,000 part-year cost of the eight coach posts into the FY2026/27 forecast, by Friday, and the cost codes to Joe today. Helena — all Executive Team members to complete Copilot Essentials before the go/no-go on Friday. Marcus — launch adverts for the eight additional coach posts, Thursday. Aisha — issue the Copilot go/no-go recommendation against the board's three conditions, Friday. Tom — find out whether Kestrel's restructure affects new starts and current learners, Friday.
Perfect. Thanks all — same time next week.

recap.summary: Three actions slipped again: the coach adverts (waiting for cost-centre codes), the phasing of the £186,000 coach cost and the COO's overdue review trajectory, now in its third week. Five of the eight Executive Team members have completed Copilot Essentials. Copilot dates stay at 2 and 16 November until Friday's go/no-go, although David Okafor is worried about the 16 November ILR clash. Overdue reviews reached 198 and QIP-07 is now Red. Northgrid's Data Analyst cohort has moved to 11 January; Valemont wants 20 AI4 places, so the coach split will be revisited next week. Kestrel has put its November starts on hold.

topics.title: Action log
topics.text: Adverts for the eight coach posts not yet live — the posts need cost-centre codes, which were waiting on budget phasing; now due Thursday 29 October. CFO to give Talent Acquisition the codes today and phase the £186,000 after P3 close. COO's trajectory slipped for a third week. Five of eight Exec members have done Copilot Essentials (Helena Marsh, David Okafor and Priya Raman outstanding).

topics.title: Copilot go/no-go preparation
topics.text: Permissions remediation 94%; restricted libraries excluded and tested; Essentials mandatory. Liam O'Connor will re-run the data access governance report on Wednesday 28 October as a final sweep. Dates remain 2 and 16 November for now; David Okafor's concern about Wave 2 clashing with the November ILR freeze goes into the go/no-go thread for Friday.

topics.title: Progress reviews
topics.text: 198 overdue progress reviews, up seven on the week. Red learners are being re-booked first and a nominated mentor can attend after two line-manager cancellations. QIP-07 was rated Red at the 23 October QIP review.

topics.title: Commercial
topics.text: Northgrid's Data Analyst cohort (12 starts) moves to 11 January 2027. Valemont wants 20 AI4 places (levy £572,000); its People Committee decides on 12 November. Kestrel Logistics has put six November starts on hold while it restructures its depots; 41 learners are on programme.

topics.title: Coach adverts and split
topics.text: Tom Whitfield asked to reopen the five Data / three Leadership split because of Valemont. Adverts will go out on Thursday without fixed numbers per academy, and the split will be revisited on 2 November.

topics.title: Finance, quality and AOB
topics.text: October funding expected to be behind budget again, mainly Data Academy. OTJ audit draft due 30 October — no ineligible claims, but catch-up plans look thin. Helena Marsh will attend the Birmingham coffee morning on 16 November.

decisions: Copilot dates remain Wave 1 Monday 2 November and Wave 2 Monday 16 November until the go/no-go on Friday 30 October, where the Wave 2 date will be reconsidered.
Coach adverts go live without fixing the number of posts per academy; the five Data / three Leadership split will be revisited on 2 November.
